arxiv-2012-11304.title: Intermittent null energy condition violations during inflation and primordial gravitational waves
arxiv-2012-11304.creator: Yong Cai 1, Yun-Song Piao 2,3,4,5
arxiv-2012-11304.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yong Cai 1, Yun-Song Piao 2,3,4,5. Primordial null energy condition (NEC) violation would imprint a blue-tilted spectrum on gravitational wave background (GWB). However, its implications on the GWB might be far richer than expected.

arxiv-2102-05413.title: Nested Sinkhorn Divergence To Compute The Nested Distance
arxiv-2102-05413.creator: Alois Pichler, Michael Weinhardt
arxiv-2102-05413.description: Abstract The nested distance builds on the Wasserstein distance to quantify the difference of stochastic processes, including also the information modelled by filtrations. The Sinkhorn divergence is a relaxation of the Wasserstein distance, which can be computed considerably faster. For this reason we employ the Sinkhorn divergence and take advantage of the related (fixed point) iteration algorithm.

arxiv-2110-06866.title: Bayesian logistic regression for online recalibration and revision of risk prediction models with guarantees
arxiv-2110-06866.creator: Jean, Romain, Alexej, Berkman
arxiv-2110-06866.description: Abstract See pages - of word.pdf Figure 1 : Given a patient with variables x , the model reviser \hat{A}_{t} wraps around an underlying ML model \hat{f}_{t} to predict the true probability of having or developing a disease (or outcome). The focus of this work is the design of an online model reviser.

arxiv-2110-15840.title: SMEFT analysis of the electroweak sector: challenges beyond dimension 6
arxiv-2110-15840.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by *. In these proceedings we present the latest developments in our effort to include vector boson scattering (VBS) measurements into global SMEFT fits of LHC data. We present some updates to our initial study of arXiv:2101.03180 as well as comment on a possible roadmap for the inclusion of higher orders beyond dimension 6 in the SMEFT and on the interpretation of VBS data in other EFT frameworks.

arxiv-2203-11869.title: An Optimal Transport Formulation of Bayes’ Law for Nonlinear Filtering Algorithms
arxiv-2203-11869.creator: Amirhossein Taghvaei, Bamdad Hosseini
arxiv-2203-11869.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Amirhossein Taghvaei, Bamdad Hosseini. This paper presents a variational representation of the Bayes’ law using optimal transportation theory. The variational representation is in terms of the optimal transportation between the joint distribution of the (state, observation) and their independent coupling. By imposing certain structure on the transport map, the solution to the variational problem is used to construct a Brenier-type map that transports the prior distribution to the posterior distribution for any value of the observation signal.

arxiv-2302-11429.title: Green’s function analysis of the Neutron Lloyd interferometer
arxiv-2302-11429.creator: Christian Käding, Mario Pitschmann, Hartmut Abele
arxiv-2302-11429.description: Abstract The neutron optical Lloyd interferometer can serve as a potent experiment for probing fundamental physics beyond the standard models of particles and cosmology. In this article, we provide a full Green’s function analysis of a Lloyd interferometer in the limit that the reflecting mirror extends to the screen.

arxiv-2305-03326.creator: Zihao Cheng, Anthony Wachs
arxiv-2305-03326.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zihao Cheng, Anthony Wachs. We present a physics-informed neural network (PINN) model to predict the hydrodynamic force and torque fluctuations in a random array of stationary bidisperse spheres. arxiv-2312-01188.title: Efficient Expansion and Gradient Based Task Inference for Replay Free Incremental Learning
arxiv-2312-01188.creator: Soumya Roy, Vinay K Verma*, Deepak Gupta
arxiv-2312-01188.description: Abstract This paper proposes a simple but highly efficient expansion-based model for continual learning. The recent feature transformation, masking and factorization-based methods are efficient, but they grow the model only over the global or shared parameter. Therefore, these approaches do not fully utilize the previously learned information because the same task-specific parameter forgets the earlier knowledge.

arxiv-2512-05371.title: ChipMind: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Long-Context Circuit Design Specifications Thanks: Corresponding author: xi.wang@seu.edu.cn
arxiv-2512-05371.creator: Changwen Xing, SamZaak Wong, Xinlai Wan, Yanfeng Lu, Mengli Zhang, Zebin Ma
arxiv-2512-05371.description: Abstract While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate immense potential for automating integrated circuit (IC) development, their practical deployment is fundamentally limited by restricted context windows. Existing context-extension methods struggle to achieve effective semantic modeling and thorough multi-hop reasoning over extensive, intricate circuit specifications.

arxiv-2601-08087.title: The Secret Lives of Open Clusters: a Multiwavelength Examination of Three Open Clusters
arxiv-2601-08087.creator: Kristen C. Dage, Emily L. Hunt, Jasmine Anderson-Baldwin, Evangelia Tremou, Khushboo K. Rao, Kwangmin Oh, Malu Sudha, Jarrod Hurley, Robert D. Mathieu, Aarya Patil, Richard M. Plotkin, Andrew M. Hopkins, Jacco Th. van Loon, Jayde Willingham
arxiv-2601-08087.description: Abstract Star clusters are well known for their dynamical interactions, an outcome of their high stellar densities; in this paper we use multiwavelength observations to search for the unique outcomes of these interactions in three nearby Galactic open clusters: IC 2602 (30 Myr), NGC 2632 (750 Myr) and M67 (4 Gyr).

pmc-11423482.creator: Jorge Eduardo Mendoza Flores, Angelica Terrazas, Alma V Lara Sagahon, Monica Aleman
pmc-11423482.description: BackgroundParasympathetic tone activity (PTA) in response to nociceptive stimulus in conscious non‐sedated horses is unknown.ObjectivesStudy PTA, heart rate (HR), and horse grimace scale (HGS) at rest and during mechanical nociceptive stimulation.AnimalsNinety healthy young adult horses (females, males): 30 each of Friesians, Quarter Horses, and Warmbloods.MethodsProspective control study.

pmc-11610132.title: Dual targeting heterodimer PET tracer [18F]AlF‑FAPI‑RGD in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a pilot exploratory study
pmc-11610132.creator: Hao Wang, Wei Su, Limeng He, Dongze Wu, Nan Liu, Jing Zhu, Jingjing Zhang, Wei Zhang
pmc-11610132.description: Purpose: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes and angiogenesis play crucial roles in the advancement of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This prospective study aimed to assess the efficacy of [18F]AlF-FAPI-RGD, a dual-targeting heterodimer tracer that focuses on fibroblast activation protein (FAP) and integrin αvβ3, through PET/CT imaging for evaluating disease activity and response to treatment in RA.

pmc-12366223.title: Spatial and temporal epidemiology of FMD in Bhutan (2011–2019)
pmc-12366223.creator: Sangay Letho, Chris Compton
pmc-12366223.description: BackgroundFoot and Mouth Disease (FMD) is an important disease in livestock in Bhutan due to its significant social and economic impacts to the farmers as well as to the government. FMD outbreaks continue to occur every year with greater frequency in some parts of the country despite the implementation of control measures.

pmc-12568357.title: Peripheral immune and metabolic regulation of Aβ and Tau by exercise in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-12568357.creator: Yuehan Yu, Kang Chen
pmc-12568357.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), characterized by the pathological accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated Tau proteins, remains a major global health challenge with limited therapeutic options. Recent findings highlight that peripheral immune and metabolic pathways play a pivotal role in regulating brain Aβ and Tau homeostasis, particularly in response to physical exercise.

pmc-12696649.title: Arsenic regulates ALKBH1 abundance and substrate specificity to promote translation and tumorigenicity
pmc-12696649.creator: Emma Wilkinson, Yan-Hong Cui, Zizhao Yang, Michelle Verghese, Seungwon Yang, Ming Sun, Houxiang Zhu, Jack Peterson, Jiangbo Wei, Yingming Zhao, Mengjie Chen, Chuan He, Yu-Ying He
pmc-12696649.description: SUMMARYThe mechanisms that underlie arsenic tumorigenicity remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that arsenic regulates the abundance and the demethylase activity of ALKBH1, which, in turn, promotes arsenic-induced skin tumorigenesis. At the molecular level, knockdown of ALKBH1 in arsenic-exposed keratinocytes increases m6A enrichment in mRNA, and ALKBH1 demethylates m6A in vitro in an arsenic-dependent manner.

pmc-13116397.title: Alcohol Intake, Cardiometabolic Risk, Fibrosis, and Gut Microbiota in Steatotic Liver Disease: A Population-Based Health Checkup Study
pmc-13116397.creator: Keisuke Furusawa, Chikara Iino, Keita Mikami, Satoshi Sato, Kenta Yoshida, Shigeyuki Nakaji, Tatsuya Mikami, Hirotake Sakuraba
pmc-13116397.description: Background: The real-world risk profiles of newly defined steatotic liver disease (SLD) subtypes—MASLD, MetALD, and ALD—remain incompletely described in community settings. Methods: A cross-sectional analysis of 950 health-checkup participants was conducted. SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m) and significant fibrosis (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa) were evaluated by transient elastography.

pmc-13277959.title: Brainstem Astrocytes Regulate Estrus‐Dependent Oscillations in Food Intake
pmc-13277959.creator: K. Selin Ozkaya, Ceyda Yalcin, Emily E. Haar, Ruchi Bhagat, Kirsteen N. Browning
pmc-13277959.description: Previous studies have shown that dorsal vagal complex (DVC) astrocytes play important roles in homeostatic regulation of food intake and caloric balance, specifically upregulation of NMDA receptor‐mediated glutamatergic signaling to brainstem dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (DMV) motoneurons restores caloric balance following exposure to caloric dense diets.

pmc-13327430.title: Barriers and Facilitators Perceived by Primary Healthcare Professionals About Physical Activity Prescription, a Meta‐Ethnography
pmc-13327430.creator: Jesus Batuecas‐Caletrio, Beatriz Rodriguez‐Martin
pmc-13327430.description: ObjectiveTo examine qualitative evidence on the barriers and facilitators perceived by Primary Health Care professionals in prescribing physical activity, using the Social Ecological Model as the analytical framework.MethodsA qualitative systematic review using a meta‐ethnographic approach was conducted. Searches were performed between 2013 and 2024 in Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, ProQuest, and The Cochrane Library Plus.

pmc-13569881.title: Development of Integrated Parent–Metabolite Pharmacokinetic Model With Apparent Presystemic Metabolism to Characterize the Disposition of Alverine
pmc-13569881.creator: Ara Cho, Hyeon‐Cheol Jeong, MinJu Kim, Inkyung Cho, Hyeon‐Jeong Na, Kyong‐Cheol Ko, Yoon‐Jee Chae, Kyeong‐Ryoon Lee
pmc-13569881.description: Alverine is an antispasmodic agent characterized by extensive metabolism, and systemic exposure is largely driven by its metabolites. However, conventional parent–metabolite pharmacokinetic models typically assume metabolite formation solely from the systemic parent compound, which may not adequately capture route‐dependent differences in metabolite exposure.

pmc-13669758.title: Unrestricted drinking before procedural sedation using fasting cards: a prospective observational quality improvement study
pmc-13669758.creator: Anne Rüggeberg, Eike A Nickel
pmc-13669758.description: Background and AimsInternational guidelines recommend clear-liquid fasting for 2 hours before procedural sedation—but in practice, this fasting time is usually exceeded, often significantly. We aimed to align actual liquid fasting times with these guidelines by implementing ‟unrestricted drinking using fasting cards” for patients undergoing procedural sedation.

pmc-13674213.title: Chemical Strategies for Multistimuli Responsive Dynamic Covalent Materials in Regenerative Medicine
pmc-13674213.creator: Saurabh Joshi, Matthew B Baker, Dominik Schauenburg
pmc-13674213.description: Regenerative medicine requires biomaterials that can function within complex and dynamically changing biological environments. Dynamic covalent chemistry provides a compelling foundation for such materials by combining covalent stability with reversible bond exchange, enabling adaptability, self‐healing, and stimulus‐responsive behavior. Dynamic covalent biomaterials have therefore emerged as promising platforms for tissue scaffolds, wound healing, and controlled delivery applications.

(a) Designation and classification of positions to be occupied; notice Not later than 15 days after February 15, 1981, the Secretary of Agriculture shall— (1) designate and classify under section 3981 of this title those positions in the Foreign Agricultural Service.
